\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{index::doc}}


\sphinxAtStartPar
CBMPy is a platform for constraint\sphinxhyphen{}based modelling and analysis of biological systems.
It implements Flux Balance Analysis (FBA), Flux Variability Analysis (FVA), and other
constraint\sphinxhyphen{}based methods using linear and mixed\sphinxhyphen{}integer programming.


\chapter{Quick Start}
\label{\detokenize{index:quick-start}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After installing CBMPy:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{cbmpy}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Read a model from SBML}
\PYG{n}{cmod} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{cbmpy}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{readSBML3FBC}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{example\PYGZus{}model.xml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Perform Flux Balance Analysis}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{cbmpy}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{doFBA}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cmod}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Print the optimal objective value}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Optimal flux: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\section{Installation Guide}
\label{\detokenize{installation:installation-guide}}\label{\detokenize{installation::doc}}

\subsection{Installing CBMPy}
\label{\detokenize{installation:installing-cbmpy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
CBMPy supports Python 3.8 through 3.12. You can install it using conda or pip.


\subsection{Prerequisites}
\label{\detokenize{installation:prerequisites}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{System Requirements:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.8 \sphinxhyphen{} 3.12

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
One of the following solvers:
\sphinxhyphen{} IBM CPLEX (commercial)
\sphinxhyphen{} GLPK (open source, via \sphinxtitleref{swiglpk})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
numpy \textgreater{}= 1.17.0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
python\sphinxhyphen{}libsbml \textgreater{}= 5.18.0 (for SBML support)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
scipy (for numerical operations)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Using Conda (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{installation:using-conda-recommended}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a conda environment:

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Activate the environment:

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
conda\PYG{+w}{ }activate\PYG{+w}{ }cbmpy3
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install CBMPy:

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
conda\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }cbmpy
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternatively, create an environment with all dependencies:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
conda\PYG{+w}{ }env\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}f\PYG{+w}{ }environment.yml
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{installation:troubleshooting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Error: “No linear solver present”}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You need to install either CPLEX or GLPK. On Linux:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install GLPK via swiglpk}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }swiglpk
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Error: “python\sphinxhyphen{}libsbml not found”}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Install python\sphinxhyphen{}libsbml:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }python\PYGZhy{}libsbml
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{On Windows with CPLEX:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download the CPLEX Python package from IBM

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add the CPLEX directory to your PYTHONPATH

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install CBMPy

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Update CBMPy}
\label{\detokenize{installation:update-cbmpy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After installation, you can update CBMPy using:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Conda}
conda\PYG{+w}{ }update\PYG{+w}{ }cbmpy

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pip}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }cbmpy
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Or update in\sphinxhyphen{}place:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}.[dev]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the fundamental circuit of an element.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If e is a non\sphinxhyphen{}basis element, the fundamental circuit, i.e. the support of the
column of e, is returned.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If e is a basis element, the cofundamental circuit, i.e. the support of the row
of e, is returned.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned fundamental circuit does not contain e itself

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{fundamentalCircuitValues() (cbmpy.fluxmodules.matroid.Matroid method)@\spxentry{fundamentalCircuitValues()}\spxextra{cbmpy.fluxmodules.matroid.Matroid method}}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{e}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the fundamental circuit of an element with the coefficients.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If e is a non\sphinxhyphen{}basis element, the fundamental circuit, i.e. the support of the
column of e, is returned.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If e is a basis element, the cofundamental circuit, i.e. the support of the row
of e, is returned.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned fundamental circuit does not contain e itself. If needed, it should

Computes a similarity matrix on the elements.

For each pair of elements the similarity matrix has an entry that
gives the similarity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
stype gives what kind of similarity matrix should be computed.
Possibilities are:
direct \sphinxhyphen{} direct from the columns of the original coefficient matrix
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
(needs the original coefficient matrix and in the case of
contractions the result is not well defined)
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\_\_cols \sphinxhyphen{} normalized from the columns (rows are orthogonal)
rows \sphinxhyphen{} normalized from the rows (columns are orthogonal)
combined \sphinxhyphen{} takes max(\_\_cols, rows)

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds the reduced representation matrix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Given a matrix of columns (self.matrix) it builds the reduced representation matrix
(self.rep) that has rows for each basis element and columns for each non\sphinxhyphen{}basis
element.

\sphinxAtStartPar
From this form the fundamental cycles can easily be read of and other operations
like deletion and contraction are easy.

\end{fulllineitems}

Bases: {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/modules:cbmpy.fluxmodules.decomposition.AbstractVertex}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AbstractVertex}}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Represents an inner vertex (i.e., not a leaf)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every Vertex contains a map (edges) of adjacent edges resp. vertices.
Each Edge has a list of elements associated to it (the interface).
Each Vertex stores a matroid, whoose elements are contributed by the edges.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The map edges has the following form:
The keys are the incident vertices.
The values are the list of elements contributed by the edge

Verifies that this branch decomposition is fully branched.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The branch decomposition is considered fully branched if all vertices
satisfy:
\sphinxhyphen{} is degree 3 or
\sphinxhyphen{} all elements are parallel
\sphinxhyphen{} all elements are coparallel

\sphinxAtStartPar
If successful, True is returned.
Otherwise, a NotFullyBranchedException is raised

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{poolmanMethod() (cbmpy.fluxmodules.decomposition.Decomposition method)@\spxentry{poolmanMethod()}\spxextra{cbmpy.fluxmodules.decomposition.Decomposition method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api/modules:cbmpy.fluxmodules.decomposition.Decomposition.poolmanMethod}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{poolmanMethod}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{vertex}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{similarity}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decomposes the matroid using the method suggested by Poolman et al.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method iteratively groups these elements together that are most similar.
Similarity by sets of nodes is done via the mean. For more details see
doi:10.1016/j.jtbi.2007.08.005

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method takes a similarity matrix as input, which allows it to also apply
the method to other similarity matrices then those suggested in the original
work. If no similarity matrix is given, then a row similarity matrix is used,
which corresponds to the matrix suggested by Poolman et al.

\end{fulllineitems}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{compartments}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Determines all reactions and flux values associated with a list of
compartments. This function can be used to find all transport reactions between
compartments, e.g. the cytosol and mitochondria. If the compartment IDs are
‘cyt’ and ‘mit’, respectively, you can call
“your\_model.getFluxesAssociatedWithCompartments({[}‘cyt’, ‘mit’{]})” to get all
fluxes between these compartments.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{compartments}: a list or set of compartment IDs.                 To check the
existing compartment IDs in your model                 call
“your\_model.getCompartmentIds()”

\sphinxAtStartPar
:returns a dictionary with reaction IDs as keys and corresponding flux values as
values

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{createSingleGeneEffectMap() (cbmpy.CBModel.Model method)@\spxentry{createSingleGeneEffectMap()}\spxextra{cbmpy.CBModel.Model method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api/core:cbmpy.CBModel.Model.createSingleGeneEffectMap}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{createSingleGeneEffectMap}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
This takes a model and analyses the logical gene expression patterns. This
only needs to be done once, the result is a dictionary that has boolean effect
patterns as keys and the (list of) genes that give rise to those patterns as
values. This map is used by the single gene deletion method for further
analysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note this dictionary can also be stored and retrieved separately as long as the
model structure is not changed i.e. the gene associations themselves or order of
reactions (stored as the special entry ‘keyJ’).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Stored as self.\_\_single\_gene\_effect\_map\_\_

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A weighted quadratic flux that appears in an objective function, this
fluxobjective contains two reaction terms to define “quadratic” fluxobjectives of
the type \textless{}coefficient\textgreater{}*\textless{}variable1\textgreater{}*\textless{}variable2\textgreater{} For example 2*R1*R2.

\sphinxAtStartPar
NOTE: reaction is a string containing a reaction id

\sphinxAtStartPar

{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads a model encoded as an Excel97 workbook and returns it as a CBMPy model object and SBML file. Note the workbook must be formatted exactly like those produced by cbm.writeModelToExcel97(). Note that reactions have to be defined in \sphinxstylestrong{both} the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaction} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{network\_react} sheets to be included in the model.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{xlpath}} \textendash{} the filename of the Excel workbook

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{return\_model}} \textendash{} {[}default=True{]} construct and return the CBMPy model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{write\_sbml}} \textendash{} {[}default=True{]} write the SBML file to fname

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{return\_dictionaries}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} return the dictionaries constructed when reading the Excel file (in place of the model)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sbml\_level}} \textendash{} {[}default=3{]} write the SBML file as either SBML L2 FBA or SBML L3 FBC file.

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Takes an FBA model object and writes it to file as SBML L3 FBC:
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{fba}} \textendash{} an fba model object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{fname}} \textendash{} the model will be written as XML to \sphinxstyleemphasis{fname}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directory}} \textendash{} {[}default=None{]} if defined it is prepended to fname

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gpr\_from\_annot}} \textendash{} {[}default=True{]} if enabled will attempt to add the gene protein associations from the annotations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{add\_groups}} \textendash{} {[}default=True{]} add SBML3 groups (if supported by libSBML)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{add\_cbmpy\_annot}} \textendash{} {[}default=True{]} add CBMPy KeyValueData annotation. Replaces \textless{}notes\textgreater{}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{add\_cobra\_annot}} \textendash{} {[}default=True{]} add COBRA \textless{}notes\textgreater{} annotation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{xoptions}} \textendash{} extended options

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{fbc\_version}} \textendash{} {[}default=1{]} write SBML3FBC using version 1 (2013) or version 2 (2015)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{validate}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} validate the output SBML file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{compress\_bounds}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} try compress output flux bound parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{zip\_model}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} compress the model using PKZIP encoding

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{return\_model\_string}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} return the SBML XML file as a string

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{fname}} \textendash{} filename\_base for the CSV output

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{work\_dir}} \textendash{} {[}default=None{]} if set the output directory for the csv files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

Check for multiply defined bounds, bounds without a reaction, inconsistent

\sphinxhyphen{} ‘eq+lb’: equality + lower bound conflicts
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘eq+ub’: equality + upper bound conflicts
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘duplicate\_ids’: duplicate flux bound IDs
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiple\_defines’: multiple bound definitions
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘lb\textgreater{}ub’: lower bound \textgreater{} upper bound
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘undefined’: bounds without values
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘rev\_contradict’: reversibility contradictions
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘no\_reaction’: bounds without a reaction

\end{description}\end{quote}

\pysigstartsignatures

{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cbmpy.CBTools.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{merge2Models}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{m1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{m2}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{ignore}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{ignore\_duplicate\_ids}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Merge two models (m2 into m1) without model checking.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Merge 2 models, this method does a raw merge of model 2 into model 1
without any model checking. Component IDs in ignore are ignored in both
models and the first objective of model 1 is arbitrarily set as active.
Compartments are also merged and a new “OuterMerge” compartment is created.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In all cases, duplicate IDs are tracked and ignored, essentially using
the object ID encountered first (usually that of model 1). Duplicate
checking can be disabled by setting the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ignore\_duplicate\_ids} flag.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{m1}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{CBMPy model}}) \textendash{} model 1 (target)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{m2}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{CBMPy model}}) \textendash{} model 2 (source)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ignore}} (\sphinxhref{https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html\#list}{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{list}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} list of IDs to skip during merge {[}default=None{]}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ignore\_duplicate\_ids}} (\sphinxhref{https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html\#bool}{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} disable duplicate ID checking {[}default=False{]}

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In development \sphinxhyphen{} merging genes and GPRs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{CBMPy model} \textendash{} the merged model

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optimize a model and add the result of the optimization to the model object (e.g. \sphinxtitleref{reaction.value}, \sphinxtitleref{objectiveFunction.value}). The stoichiometric matrix is automatically generated. This is a common function available in all solver interfaces. By default returns the objective function value.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{f}} \textendash{} an instantiated PySCeSCBM model object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lpFname}} \textendash{} {[}default=None{]} the name of the intermediate LP file saved when this has a string value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{return\_lp\_obj}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} off by default when enabled it returns the PyGLPK LP object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{with\_reduced\_costs}} \textendash{} {[}default=’scaled’{]} calculate and add reduced cost information to mode this can be: ‘unscaled’ or ‘scaled’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{with\_sensitivity}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} add solution sensitivity information (not yet implemented)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{del\_intermediate}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} delete the intermediary files after updating model object, useful for server applications

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{build\_n}} \textendash{} {[}default=True{]} generate stoichiometry from the reaction network (reactions/reagents/species)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{quiet}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} suppress glpk output

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{oldlpgen}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} not used anymore

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} \textendash{} {[}default=’s’{]} select the GLPK solver method, see the GLPK documentation for details

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

Reads a model encoded as an Excel97 workbook and returns it as a CBMPy model object and SBML file. Note the workbook must be formatted exactly like those produced by cbm.writeModelToExcel97(). Note that reactions have to be defined in \sphinxstylestrong{both} the \sphinxstyleemphasis{reaction} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{network\_react} sheets to be included in the model.

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{return\_model}} \textendash{} {[}default=True{]} construct and return the CBMPy model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{names}} \textendash{} FluxVariabilityAnalysis() FVA OUTPUT\_NAMES

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{fname}} \textendash{} filename\_base for the CSV output

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{work\_dir}} \textendash{} {[}default=None{]} if set the output directory for the csv files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{roundec}} \textendash{} {[}default=None{]} an integer indicating at which decimal to round off output. Default is no rounding.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{appendfile}} \textendash{} {[}default=False{]} instead of opening a new file try and append the data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{minHeight} {[}default=None{]} the minimum length that defined a span

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{maxHeight} {[}default=None{]} the maximum length a span can obtain, bar will be limited to maxHeight and coloured yellow

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{roundec} {[}default=None{]} an integer indicating at which decimal to round off output. Default is no rounding.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{autoclose} {[}default=True{]} autoclose plot after save

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{fluxval} {[}default=True{]} plot the flux value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{type} {[}default=’png’{]} the output format, depends on matplotlib backend e.g. ‘png’, ‘pdf’, ‘eps’

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}

\section{0.8.9 (unreleased)}
\label{\detokenize{release-notes:unreleased}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Docstring improvements:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Converted all module docstrings to numpy format across the entire codebase
\sphinxhyphen{} CBXML.py: 68 docstrings converted
\sphinxhyphen{} CBModel.py: 206 docstrings converted
\sphinxhyphen{} CBCPLEX.py: 25 docstrings converted
\sphinxhyphen{} CBGLPK.py: 16 docstrings converted
\sphinxhyphen{} CBNetDB.py: 21 docstrings converted
\sphinxhyphen{} CBRead.py: 6 docstrings converted
\sphinxhyphen{} CBWrite.py: 31 docstrings converted

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All docstrings now use numpy format compatible with Sphinx Napoleon extension

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sphinx documentation updated with all documented modules

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Improvements:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Updated Sphinx docs with new module API pages
\sphinxhyphen{} api/solvers.rst \sphinxhyphen{} CBSolver, CBSolverX, CBCPLEX, CBGLPK, CBGLPKOLD
\sphinxhyphen{} api/io.rst \sphinxhyphen{} CBRead, CBReadtxt, CBWrite, CBXML
\sphinxhyphen{} api/networking.rst \sphinxhyphen{} CBNetDB, miriamids
\sphinxhyphen{} api/visualization.rst \sphinxhyphen{} CBPlot, GUI frontends, multi\sphinxhyphen{}processing, utilities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Added missing core classes to docs (Species, Objective, GeneProteinAssociation, UserConstraint, Group)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fixed docstring style reference in CLAUDE.md (numpydoc \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} numpy)

\end{itemize}
